Perenti Ltd Launches $120 Million Expansion to Boost Australian Mining Services

Perenti Ltd, a leading player in Australia’s metals and mining sector, has announced a $120 million investment to expand its mining services operations across Western Australia and Queensland. The move is set to strengthen the company’s position in the nation’s booming resources industry and comes as demand for critical minerals continues to rise globally.

The new capital will be allocated towards fleet expansion, advanced drilling technology, and workforce development initiatives, according to a statement released by Perenti Ltd on Thursday. The company will also upgrade its training facilities in Kalgoorlie and Mackay to support the recruitment and upskilling of over 200 new employees.

“We are excited to take this next step in our growth journey,” said Mark Ashton, Perenti Ltd’s Chief Executive Officer. “This investment not only enhances our capacity to deliver innovative mining solutions but also reinforces our long-term commitment to the regions where we operate.”

The expansion will see Perenti Ltd add 15 new drill rigs and 40 haul trucks to its fleet over the next 18 months. The company will also invest in digital optimisation tools to improve operational efficiency and sustainability, reflecting growing industry emphasis on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) standards.

Industry analysts welcomed the news, noting that the expansion positions Perenti Ltd to capitalise on robust market conditions. “With global demand for lithium, nickel, and copper at record highs, this is a timely move,” said Fiona Jones, a mining sector analyst at Wilshire Partners. “Perenti Ltd’s investment in cutting-edge equipment and workforce training will help them capture a greater share of upcoming projects, particularly in battery metals.”

The Australian Resources and Mining Association (ARMA) also applauded the initiative, highlighting the potential benefits for regional employment. “Expansions like this generate significant economic activity and career opportunities, especially in mining communities,” said ARMA President Greg Liu. “We look forward to seeing the positive impact on local suppliers and job seekers.”

Perenti Ltd indicated that it aims to increase its service capacity by 25% by the end of 2025, with a particular focus on open-pit and underground mining contracts. The company is currently engaged in several long-term projects across the Pilbara and Bowen Basin, and expects the expansion to support new contract wins.

“Our customers are seeking partners who can deliver efficiently and sustainably,” Ashton added. “This investment ensures we’re ready to meet that challenge and support the future of Australian mining.”

Shares of Perenti Ltd closed up 1.4% on Thursday following the announcement.
